organisation_name: HelpAge Ethiopia is a network member of HelpAge International, a global network of organizations working towards a fairer world for older people so they can live safe, healthy, and dignified lives. In addition to working with more than 170 network members in 91 countries, HelpAge International operates country program offices in 13 countries across Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Eastern Europe. Over the years, the HelpAge International Ethiopia office has been engaging in various service provision activities including humanitarian and development assistance. HelpAge International has also played a key role in promoting the rights of older people and building the capacity of partners and stakeholders for sustainable change. These include setting up of advocacy framework and coordinating higher-level policy dialogues; strengthening the capacity of age- inclusive organizations and older people groups to own and demonstrate actions on and supporting consultative process between OPAs and CSO partners on a list of priority issues and agendas, facilitating them to take lead on the day-to-day implementation of project activities at local, district and regional levels. HelpAge International Ethiopia country program enjoys excellent rapport with the National and Local Government Authorities in Ethiopia including the Ministry of Health, Ministry of Women and Social Affairs, The Refugees and Returnees Service, Authority for Civil Society Organizations, and Regional Administration and Local Government structures. The country program also works with Government Institutions, Research/Academic Institutions, UN agencies, Network members, and Local partners based in Ethiopia. HelpAge International Ethiopia country program’s current focus areas are Income security, Healthy Ageing, and Inclusive Humanitarian Action. More specifically, our sectoral interventions address social protection, health and wellbeing, nutrition,voice/advocacy, livelihoods, protection, and inclusion in both humanitarian and development contexts. In line with its organizational commitment to the Charter for Change, a key element of the HelpAge International Global Strategy 2030, HelpAge International has been transitioning all country programs to be locally led and managed by national 2024/25. To this end, HelpAge International`s country office in Ethiopia has been undergoing a series of consultations for the past 3 years with stakeholders` including target beneficiaries to figure out the best option to embrace localization ambition.

organisation_name: Vision A future where Ethiopian women and girls fully exercise their rights, experience gender justice, and thrive in an equitable society. Mission To advance gender equality and build an equitable society for Ethiopian women and girls by delivering multi-dimensional programs in education, SRHR, skills development, community engagement, and advocacy, while leveraging strategic partnerships and innovative solutions in digitalization, science, and technology. EWDO Goal To contribute to an equitable, inclusive, and resilient society where women and girls, including vulnerable and older women, fully exercise their rights, live free from violence and discrimination, and actively participate in social and economic development with dignity and equal opportunity. EWDO Objectives 1. Digital Inclusion and Empowerment for Women and Girls: - EWDO works to close the digital gender gap by increasing women’s and girls’ access to technology, digital skills, and online opportunities. The pillar also promotes online safety and addresses technology-facilitated violence; ensuring digital spaces support education, livelihoods, and empowerment. 2. Specialized GBV Prevention, Response, and Access to Justice: To prevent and respond to gender-based violence (GBV) and harmful practices by strengthening survivor-centered services, protection systems, access to justice, and community awareness. 3. Access to Comprehensive Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR): To improve equitable access to comprehensive sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) information and services, particularly for marginalized and underserved women and girls. 4. Socio-Economic Empowerment and Leadership: EWDO strengthens women’s economic independence through skills development, entrepreneurship, and digital inclusion including elder people, marginalized and underserved groups. The pillar also promotes women’s leadership across sectors, enabling them to influence economic and social decision-making. 5. Peace, Governance, and Humanitarian Action: EWDO supports active participation of women and vulnerable groups in peace building, governance, and humanitarian response. The organization advocates for gender-responsive systems and uses innovative and digital approaches to ensure women’s voices and needs are central in crisis and recovery efforts. 6. Organizational Excellence and Sustainable Impact: To strengthen institutional capacity, partnerships, innovation, and evidence-based programming to ensure sustainable impact and organizational excellence.

organisation_name: Vision: A just, inclusive, and resilient society where all people, particularly those facing poverty, exclusion, or vulnerability, have equal opportunities to access essential services, participate in decision-making, and live with dignity. Mission: Friends Foundation works to improve the well-being of underserved communities by facilitating access to quality healthcare, education, water and sanitation services, humanitarian assistance, and opportunities for social and economic development. Through community engagement, capacity building, and partnerships with public and private sector stakeholders, the organization promotes sustainable solutions that strengthen resilience and improve quality of life. Objectives and Goals: The Foundation seeks to improve access to primary healthcare, maternal and child health, nutrition, and preventive health services for disadvantaged populations. It promotes safe water, sanitation, and hygiene practices to improve public health outcomes and community well-being. The organization supports women, youth, older persons, persons with disabilities, and other marginalized groups by creating opportunities for participation, capacity development, and social inclusion. It works to strengthen community resilience to disasters and emergencies through preparedness, risk reduction, relief, and recovery initiatives. Friends Foundation also contributes to improved governance, civic engagement, and community participation by strengthening local institutions and promoting accountability and inclusion. Across all programmes, the organization focuses on building local capacities, encouraging community ownership, and supporting sustainable development that delivers long-term benefits for vulnerable populations. Website: www.ffpak.org.pk Strategic Focus Areas: Integrated Health, WASH, Women Empowerment, Climate Resilience, Education, Governance, and Humanitarian Response & Rehabilitation.
